title: Italian ski great Federica Brignone retires after remarkable injury comeback to win 2 Olympic titles
summary: Federica Brignone's stunning comeback to win two Olympic titles on home Italian snow this year after serious injury turned out to be quite a career swansong. The 36-year-old retired on Wednesday.

image.caption: Italy's Federica Brignone, one of the greatest skiers of this generation, announced her retirement Wednesday in Rome at age 36, citing ongoing pain from her left leg that she broke last year. (Stefano Rellandini/AFP via Getty Images/File)

blocks.text: Federica Brignone's stunning comeback to win two Olympic titles on home Italian snow this year after serious injury turned out to be quite a career swansong. The 36-year-old retired on Wednesday.
'My leg is not fully recovered ... I'm still in too much pain,' says 37-time World Cup winner
Federica Brignone's stunning comeback to win two Olympic titles on home Italian snow this year after serious injury turned out to be quite a career swansong.

One of the greatest skiers of this generation announced her retirement Wednesday in Rome at age 36, citing ongoing pain from her left leg that she broke last year, 10 months before the Milano-Cortina Winter Games.

Brignone's remarkable career of two overall World Cup titles, five Olympic medal — including gold in super-G and giant slalom at Cortina-d'Ampezzo in February — 37 World Cup race wins and five world championship medals will formally end with a farewell race soon.
"I would like to open the starting gate one last time, to say goodbye to this sport that I love so much and to all of you," Brignone wrote in an Instagram post. "I'll let you know where and when."
When Brignone won the second of her overall World Cup titles, the sport's most prized all-around accolade, in 2025 she seemed set to be a home team star at the 2026 Winter Olympics.
Then weeks later she broke multiple bones in her left leg crashing at the season-ending national championships and Olympic ambitions seemed over.
Brignone was unable to walk for three months and her return to ski racing was pushed back deep into the Olympic season.

blocks.text: Somehow, with just two prep races on the World Cup circuit in January, Brignone got to the Olympics and did not just start but starred.
Now, the injury has proved too much to consider another season on the tiring World Cup circuit where she also was overall champion in 2020.

"After these two days on the snow, I've realized that my leg is not fully recovered yet and that I'm still in too much pain," Brignone wrote Wednesday. "For this reason, I've decided to bring my competitive career to an end.
"It has certainly been a very difficult decision, but despite doing everything I could to get back on track, the severity of my injury simply won't allow me to do so."
